sentences.text: Telmatornis is a valid genus of prehistoric birds belonging to the order Charadriiformes.
The type species of this genus is Telmatornis priscus.
A 2002 analysis of the forelimb skeleton found Telmatornis to be highly similar to the great crested grebe.
The bird possessed a humerus dorsal condyle that was not angled 20 to 30 degrees away from the long axis of the bone.
This animal lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically the Maastrichtian age, in what is now New Jersey.
Its time range spans from the Maastrichtian to the Danian, between 72.2 and 61.66 million years ago.

There is ongoing uncertainty regarding the precise taxonomic placement of Telmatornis. It is debated whether Telmatornis was evolutionarily related to grebes or if its wing structure was merely a case of convergent evolution.
